summary.detailed_summary: STEAM addresses the challenge of EEG data heterogeneity through a dual-branch spatio-temporal encoder and a shared Soft Mixture-of-Experts (SSMoE) module that aligns spatial and temporal features. The model employs a hierarchical pre-training strategy, moving from general initialization via masked reconstruction and contrastive alignment to paradigm-specific specialization. This approach allows for efficient downstream adaptation by updating only a small fraction of parameters, significantly improving performance across various EEG decoding tasks.

headline_results: Achieved the best average rank across 14 evaluation settings compared to other EEG-FMs.
Demonstrated superior performance in cross-subject and cross-dataset scenarios.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: STEAM utilizes a dual-branch encoder with SSMoE for spatio-temporal alignment.
Hierarchical pre-training: Employs a two-stage process (General-to-Paradigm) to handle cross-dataset variability.
Efficient adaptation: Achieves state-of-the-art results by updating only 5.1% of model parameters for downstream tasks.
limitations: Computational overhead associated with the Mixture-of-Experts architecture.
Dependence on the availability of large-scale paradigm-specific data for Stage-II pre-training.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper introduces SW-ProxyCE, a framework designed to exploit the shared representation space of public EEG foundation models to attack private downstream models. By utilizing a small labeled reference set and a public encoder, the method constructs shrinkage-whitened class prototypes to derive a proxy cross-entropy objective. This allows the generation of adversarial examples without requiring any queries to the victim model or the training of a surrogate classifier. Evaluation across multiple EEG tasks and encoders demonstrates that SW-ProxyCE effectively transfers to both linear-probing and full-fine-tuning downstream models.

headline_results: SW-ProxyCE outperforms task-agnostic representation-shift attacks in transferability to private downstream models.

key_points: Method for adversarial attack: SW-ProxyCE enables zero-query transfer attacks from public EEG foundation encoders to private downstream models.
Uses shrinkage-whitened class prototypes to derive a proxy classification objective from limited labeled reference data.
limitations: Requires a small labeled reference set of the target task.
Effectiveness depends on the availability of a public encoder that shares representation space with the victim.

method.finetuning: Targets downstream models adapted via Linear Probing or Full Fine-Tuning
method.pretraining: Utilizes pre-trained public EEG foundation models

summary.detailed_summary: ZIPBrain addresses the quadratic complexity of Transformer-based EEG foundation models by introducing a redundancy-aware token pooling module. It identifies redundant tokens using L2-norm pivot selection and cosine similarity, merging them into unique tokens via norm-preserving pooling to prevent feature attenuation. The method is training-free and plug-and-play, demonstrating significant reductions in inference time and memory usage across multiple EFMs while maintaining or improving classification accuracy.

headline_results: Average accuracy improvement of 1.3% to 10.5% over baselines
LaBraM on TUAB preserved 99.65% accuracy at ~80% compression ratio

key_points: New method: ZIPBrain reduces inference latency by up to 32.7% across various EEG foundation models.
Implements norm-preserving pooling to avoid the feature attenuation common in standard averaging.
Demonstrates compatibility with multiple architectures including LaBraM, EEGPT, BIOT, and TFM-Tokenizer.
limitations: Performance gains may vary depending on the inherent redundancy of the specific EEG dataset
The method is specifically designed for Transformer-based encoders and may not apply to other architectures

method.objective: Token sequence compression via redundancy-aware pooling

summary.one_liner: A training-free, redundancy-aware token pooling module designed to reduce the computational overhead of EEG foundation models without sacrificing accuracy.

summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a training-free, norm-preserving token pooling mechanism that reduces EEG sequence length by identifying and merging redundant tokens based on L2-norm and cosine similarity.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes the Brain Latent Predictive Model (BLPM), which treats EEG decoding as a continuous semantic embedding prediction task rather than discrete token generation. It introduces a Continuous EEG Latent Predictive (CELP) encoder for self-supervised pretraining and a Multi-Query Semantic Decomposition (MQSD) module to align EEG features with language semantics. Evaluation across seven diverse benchmarks using NeuralBench shows that BLPM outperforms existing foundation models while operating as a single unified model without task-specific heads.

headline_results: Outperforms BIOT, LaBraM, CBraMod, REVE, and LUNA across multiple benchmarks as a unified model.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: BLPM uses a continuous latent predictive approach to align EEG signals with language semantics.
Introduces the MQSD module to decompose EEG representations into task-relevant semantic components using language queries.
Demonstrates superior performance across seven diverse EEG benchmarks using a unified model architecture.
limitations: Dependence on high-quality language-EEG aligned pairs for instruction tuning.
Computational overhead of the MQSD cross-attention mechanism.

method.finetuning: Multi-task instruction tuning using semantic embeddings of target answers.

method.pretraining: Self-supervised latent predictive pretraining on TUEG corpus.

summary.detailed_summary: EEG-PRISM is a model-agnostic framework designed to enhance the interpretability of EEG foundation models by translating time-channel attribution scores into spectral and spatial domains. By utilizing linear transformations and backpropagation rules, it maps attribution maps from post-hoc explainers (like Grad-CAM or SHAP) into frequency-domain biomarkers via invertible DFT and into source-domain localizations via an approximately invertible EEG generative model. The method was validated across five different foundation models and four explainers, showing high accuracy in recovering simulated biomarkers and identifying clinically relevant regions in epilepsy and autism datasets.

headline_results: Near-perfect spectral recovery in simulated data

key_points: New method: Maps time-channel attribution scores to spectral and spatial domains using linear transformations.
Demonstrated effectiveness across 5 foundation models and 4 explainers on simulated and clinical data.
Successfully localized seizure onset zones in epilepsy and identified delta-alpha biomarkers in autism.
limitations: Spatial localization depends on the quality of the approximately invertible generative model.
Performance varies depending on the choice of the initial post-hoc explainer used.
summary.one_liner: A universal post-hoc framework to map EEG foundation model attribution scores from time-channel space to physiologically meaningful spectral and spatial domains.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes tPoE-EIB, a downstream adaptation head for frozen EEG foundation models that enforces an 'evidence-only' prediction constraint. Unlike standard heads that use unrestricted hidden states, tPoE-EIB routes predictions through gated temporal and channel summaries fused via a tempered product-of-experts posterior. Evaluation across six diagnosis tasks using CodeBrain and CBraMod backbones shows that the method maintains competitive accuracy while significantly improving auditability and faithfulness compared to post-hoc explainers.

headline_results: Maintained competitive Balanced Accuracy (BAcc) compared to unrestricted heads.
Significantly improved faithfulness in audits (insertion-deletion, gate-causality) over post-hoc explainers.

key_points: Method for auditable EEG diagnosis: proposes tPoE-EIB, a bottleneck head that restricts classifiers to predict only from gated temporal and channel evidence.
Novel fusion mechanism: uses a tempered product-of-experts posterior to integrate Gaussian experts, mitigating overconfidence from correlated evidence axes.
Extensive validation: demonstrates competitive balanced accuracy and superior faithfulness across six clinical tasks using CodeBrain and CBraMod backbones.
limitations: Dependence on the quality of the frozen foundation model's latent representations.
Potential trade-off between strict auditability and maximum possible predictive accuracy.

method.finetuning: Training of the tPoE-EIB head for specific downstream diagnosis tasks.

summary.detailed_summary: INCEPT (INvariance-oriented Contextual EEG Pre-Training) addresses the limitations of reconstruction-centered pre-training in EEG foundation models, which often capture irrelevant noise. It employs a dual-objective strategy: masked contextual learning to capture local temporal, spectral, and cross-channel dependencies, and invariance learning to ensure stability across correlated observations. To handle varying electrode montages, it uses spherical-harmonics-based electrode embeddings. The model was pre-trained on the TUEG corpus and evaluated across 10 datasets covering signal-level, brain-state, and brain-health tasks, demonstrating superior performance in both linear probing and full fine-tuning scenarios.

headline_results: Ranked 1st among recent EFMs on 26/30 linear-probing metrics
Ranked 1st among recent EFMs on 24/30 fine-tuning metrics

key_points: New EEG foundation model: INCEPT uses invariance-oriented pre-training to filter nuisance variability.
Utilizes spherical-harmonics-based electrode embeddings to achieve flexibility across different EEG montages.
Outperforms existing EFMs on 26/30 linear-probing and 24/30 fine-tuning metrics across 10 diverse datasets.
limitations: Dependence on the quality and diversity of the TUEG corpus for generalizability
Computational cost associated with large-scale pre-training on 11,000 hours of data

method.finetuning: Evaluated via linear probing (frozen backbone) and full fine-tuning
method.objective: Combined masked contextual learning and invariance learning
method.pretraining: Pre-trained on TUEG corpus using masked and invariance objectives

summary.detailed_summary: The paper investigates parameter-efficient self-supervised (SSL) adaptation of pretrained EEG-FMs (BIOT and CBraMod) to bridge distribution shifts in clinical settings. By updating only the final encoder layer using the original SSL objective on unlabeled target data, the authors demonstrate significant gains over linear probing across three clinical datasets. Results show that peak performance is achieved with only 20-50% of available unlabeled data under a fixed compute budget and is driven by total window diversity rather than patient count.

headline_results: Up to 20x AUCPR improvement on rare events compared to linear probing
Peak performance reached with 20-50% of unlabeled data

key_points: Method for EEG-FM adaptation: uses parameter-efficient self-supervised learning to align pretrained models to target clinical domains by updating only the final encoder layer.
Strong evidence of efficiency: achieves peak performance using 20-50% of unlabeled data and shows that total window count is more critical than patient diversity.
Significant performance gains: improves AUCPR by up to 20x on rare-event seizure detection compared to frozen linear probing.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to a specific set of clinical datasets
Computational budget constraints were simulated and may vary across hardware

method.finetuning: Parameter-efficient update of the final encoder layer followed by linear probing
